extracted.intended_audience: researchers invited to peer review manuscripts / academic peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academics and researchers on how to perform high-quality peer reviews of research manuscripts, covering when to accept/decline, tone and content of feedback, and reviewer conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness and balance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive evaluation that fairly weighs strengths and weaknesses of the work rather than offering superficial or one‑sided comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to review invitations promptly (see 'say no promptly — within a day'); request extensions early if you need more time. Timely reviews help editors manage the process and authors progress their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn to decline appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Say no promptly — within a day of receiving an invitation; suggest alternative experts, especially early‑career researchers; request extensions early if you need more time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declining quickly allows editors to find replacements; when declining, recommend suitable alternative reviewers (including early‑career researchers) and indicate if you can review later with an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear, specific feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague comments don't help authors or editors. "Honestly and clearly state the pros and cons" and explain your reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about what is strong or weak and why. Point to exact sections, data, or claims when possible so authors know what to address; avoid vague statements that cannot be acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify suggested experiments and assess feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When suggesting experiments, justify why they're necessary and assess feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the purpose of any recommended additional work and consider the authors' likely resource constraints; acknowledge alternative ways authors might address the concern and avoid asking for unnecessary or impractical experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider your reputation / professional conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals keep identities confidential, but editors know who you are; some journals publicly credit reviewers — behave professionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a professional tone and constructive approach in reviews because your behavior can affect your reputation with editors, journals, and the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a collaborative mindset
rubrics_metrics.description: View peer review as teamwork between authors, reviewers, and editors; treat editors as partners, not just gatekeepers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your experience as an author to provide constructive, helpful guidance aimed at improving the paper and facilitating editorial decisions rather than simply blocking publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Be "timely, thoughtful, and above all empathic." Remember what feedback felt like when you were on the receiving end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques with empathy: consider the author's perspective, avoid unnecessarily harsh language, and aim to be helpful so feedback is more likely to be received and acted upon.
